instruction: We act for Vaikiv Therapeutics, Inc., the buyer in a proposed asset purchase from Taigon Pharma Holdings, LLC. Before we go back to the other side, I need a clear picture of where the current document set leaves Vaikiv exposed or falls short of what a buyer should expect. Please review everything in the matter folder: the asset purchase agreement (asset_purchase_agreement.md), the indemnity escrow agreement (indemnity_escrow_agreement.md), the seller disclosure schedule (seller_disclosure_schedule.md), the transition services agreement (transition_services_agreement.md), and the draft closing press release (closing_press_release.md). Then prepare a memo to me. For each issue you identify, state where it appears (document and section), explain why it matters to Vaikiv, and give a recommended fix, with proposed language where that would help. Put the most significant points first. If anything needs input from the client or business team before we can settle a position, flag it separately at the end. Keep the memo practical. I'll use it to plan our markup and our next call with Taigon's counsel.

rubric.text: The response concludes that, because the APA ties survival to the Escrow Agreement's Release Date, which is set at 90 days after the Closing Date, Seller's non-fundamental representations (including the regulatory or product-quality representations) survive only about 90 days after Closing.
The response locates the survival issue in APA Section 9.1 and/or Escrow Agreement Section 4.1.
The response explains why the 90-day survival cut-off matters to Vaikiv.
The response recommends a fix for the 90-day survival cut-off.

The response concludes that the TSA's choice of New York law and New York courts for disputes relating to the TSA or the Purchase Agreement conflicts with the APA's choice of Delaware law and the exclusive Delaware Court of Chancery forum.
The response locates the governing law and forum conflict in TSA Section 9.3.
The response explains why the governing law and forum conflict matters to Vaikiv.
The response recommends a fix for the governing law and forum conflict between the TSA and the APA.
hints: delete the reference to the Purchase Agreement

rubric.text: The response concludes that Disclosure Schedule 2.4(c) subjects Liabilities from the known pre-closing Oravexin recall to the indemnity cap and deductible, even though Excluded Liabilities are otherwise carved out of them.
hints: subject to the Cap and the Deductible

rubric.text: The response locates the recall cap issue in Schedule 2.4(c) of the Seller Disclosure Schedule.
The response explains why capping the recall Liabilities matters to Vaikiv.
The response recommends a fix for the Schedule 2.4(c) language that caps the recall Liabilities.
The response states that under the APA's order of precedence, each Ancillary Agreement controls matters arising under it (an exception to the APA prevailing).
The response states that the Purchase Price is $186,000,000.
The response is a memo to the supervising partner that addresses issues individually, giving for each a location, why it matters and a recommended fix.
The response includes a separate section at or near the end that flags points needing input from the client or business team.
The response claims that, under the current documents, Liabilities from the pre-closing Oravexin recall are fully uncapped and not subject to the deductible.
The response claims that, under the current documents, APA Section 11.4 makes the APA's Delaware law and forum provisions override TSA Section 9.3 for all disputes, so no conflict exists.
